reason: issue #251 selecting and editing a run of notes: the editor edited one note at a time, and setDurationType had no <time-modification> guard while setDots did, so retyping a tuplet member silently wrote a bar that no longer summed. The eleven tests: shift+ArrowRight extends the selection to the next note in the run and the render marks BOTH heads (one marker per selected ordinal, at different places on the staff), and shift+ArrowLeft walks the moving end back; the extension crosses a bar line within one voice and STOPS at a rest, the note after the rest never joining the selection; the extension stops at a voice change, asserted on the polyphonic fixture where a voice block ends mid-bar; a duration change over a three-note selection (a quarter and two 16ths, 720 divisions, retyped to three eighths) changes all three, leaves the bar summing to the same 1920, and is undone by ONE undo with nothing left to undo after it; Backspace over a selection turns each selected note into a rest keeping its own duration so the bar is unchanged, and one undo brings all three back; a tuplet member's duration type is refused with the same message shape its dots already were, the document untouched and not dirty; a range duration change containing a tuplet member is refused WHOLE, so even the note that could have taken it is untouched and no undo entry is pushed; a string change moves every note in the selection in one undo step, re-pitched from the new string's tuning; Escape collapses a range to its anchor and a plain arrow collapses and steps from the anchor; a typed fret acts on the anchor alone and leaves the range standing; and a range edit saves through the transcription PUT with the three retyped durations, every octave inside MusicXML's 0-9 and the tuplet members untouched, and is still there after a full page reload.
